transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squeal that happens only at start-up and then disappears is very typical of a worn jockey pulley (the tensioner wheel) or a belt that has glazed over. When the drum starts moving, friction heats these parts slightly, allowing them to grip properly so the noise stops. To help narrow this down, could you please unplug the dryer and turn the drum by hand? I need to know if it feels rough or squeaks when turned manually, which would point towards bearings or rollers, or if it spins freely, which points more strongly to the belt/pulley system.
I unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns, but there's a slight squeak/scrape and it feels a little rough.

[Heading: Worn drum support rollers or idler pulley]
That slight roughness and squeak when turning by hand confirms there is friction in the drum support system. Since the noise at start-up disappears once things warm up, this strongly suggests worn drum support rollers or a dry/idler pulley rather than a seized bearing (which would feel much harder to turn). To pinpoint which part needs replacing: with the dryer still unplugged, can you reach inside and try to wiggle the drum up and down gently? If there is significant play or a grinding sensation when you move it manually, that confirms worn support rollers. If it feels tight but still squeaks when turned, it points more towards the idler pulley or belt.
I'm not sure how to check that, sorry. I can't lift or tilt the dryer because of my back, and I'm not sure how to wiggle the drum from inside. Is there another way to tell?

[Heading: Worn drum support rollers or dry idler pulley]
Since you can't safely lift or tilt the machine due to your back, we won't be able to do any further internal checks. The combination of the initial squeal at startup that fades away, plus the slight roughness and squeak when turning by hand, strongly points to worn drum support rollers or a dry idler pulley. These parts wear down over time and need replacement, which involves taking the dryer apart. Because this requires dismantling the cabinet and handling heavy components, it is not an owner-safe repair. You should contact a qualified appliance engineer to replace the rollers and/or pulley. In the meantime, you can continue using it as normal, but be aware that if a roller fails completely, the drum might become harder to turn or could damage the belt.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The model number is IDC8T3B. Can you check if a replacement part is available?

[Heading: Worn drum support rollers or idler pulley]
I cannot check specific part availability or compatibility for model IDC8T3B. However, based on your description of the initial squeal that fades away and the slight roughness when turning by hand, the issue is almost certainly worn drum support rollers or a dry idler pulley. As discussed, replacing these parts requires dismantling the machine, which is not safe to do without professional tools and expertise. You will need to contact a qualified appliance engineer to perform this repair.
